content.text: ▪︎PUD: break in mucosa extending through muscularis mucosae (stomach & duodenum)
H. pylori MC cause of gastritis
▪︎H. pylori assoc dz: gastritis, gastric & duodenal ulcers, gastric adenocarcinoma, MALToma
•ETOH, smoking, stress (burns, trauma, surgery, severe medical illness); males, elderly, steroids, gastric cancer
▪︎PE often norm; ± mild epigastric TTP; labs norm unless anemia 2/2 bleeding ulcer
▪︎Sx for wks → resolve for mo-yrs → recur
▪︎DU: nocturnal pain (awakens pt); postprandial pain w/ 2-5hr delay
▪︎GU: pain 1-2hrs after meals; DU: pain often worse b4 meals
▪︎DU: younger (MC 30-55yo); GU: older (MC 55-70yo); epigastric pain in 80-90%; anorexia & N may occur w/ GU
PUD = MC cause of upper GI bleed
▪︎bleed may present as hematochezia, melena, or new-onset aSx iron deficiency anemia

▪︎noninvasive testing 1st if <60yo & ⍉alarm sx (dysphagia, wt loss, anemia); empiric tx failure → endoscopy
(H. pylori converts labeled urea → labeled CO2; breathing out labeled urea = +)
▪︎fecal Ag (94% sens/98% spec); C13 UBT (98/96); serology (85/79)
▪︎bismuth quadruple = ACG 1st-line (⍉affected by clarithromycin resistance, which has ↓ triple-therapy efficacy); ~85% eradication
▪︎rifabutin triple (omeprazole + amoxicillin + rifabutin): alternative for tx-experienced/refractory, esp after bismuth quadruple failure
▪︎triple therapy: omeprazole + clarithromycin + amoxicillin (metro if PCN-allergic)
▪︎clarithromycin-based triple ⍉appropriate as empiric 1st-line in most US settings (⇡ macrolide resistance)
▪︎test for cure (UBT or fecal Ag) ≥4wks after completing regimen
▪︎d/c offending agents + PPI trial 4-8wks; adding sucralfate or H2 blocker also aids healing
▪︎duodenal gastrinoma or non-beta islet cell (islet of Langerhans) → gastrin → parietal cell → HCl → ulcer formation; most pts develop peptic ulcers
Abd pain, chronic diarrhea, dyspepsia, wt loss, GI bleeding
Gastric pH >3.0 implies hypochlorhydria & excludes gastrinoma
= spiral-shaped gram-⍉ rod; colonizes gastric mucosa; person-to-person spread
▪︎MC cause of PUD & chronic gastritis; long-term PPI use assoc w/ ↑risk H. pylori gastritis
▪︎assoc dz: gastritis, gastric & duodenal ulcers, gastric adenocarcinoma, MALToma
▪︎chronic H. pylori gastritis → ↑risk gastric & duodenal ulcers; extraintestinal: IDA (⇣ iron absorption from gastric atrophy & hypochlorhydria, gastric pH >3.0), ITP, vit B12 deficiency
Most commonly aSx; when Sx present → gastritis/PUD-like: dyspepsia, N/V, epigastric pain
▪︎acute: aSx or mild N, abd pain, or dyspepsia x several days; if untreated → most become chronic gastritis
(noninvasive; testing 1st if <60yo & ⍉alarm sx); hold abx, PPIs & bismuth b4 testing; d/c PPIs 7–14d b4 UBT & fecal Ag

▪︎endoscopy w/ bx: mucosal erythema, friable gastric mucosa, diffuse antral nodularity; rapid urease test for active H. pylori; histology = definitive dx (also → severity/extent & comp: intestinal metaplasia, MALT lymphoma, gastric carcinoma)
▪︎triple therapy: omeprazole + clarithromycin + amoxicillin (metro if PCN-allergic); clarithromycin-based triple ⍉appropriate as empiric 1st-line in most US settings (⇡ macrolide resistance)
